# Data Sketch

> Practical data engineering diagrams by Mario Caesar, with short lessons on SQL joins, backfills, data quality checks, and warehouse workflows.

Canonical site: https://datasketch.caesarmar.io/. Use the lesson sources below for factual summaries. Upcoming episodes are not published sources.

## Primary pages

- [Data Sketch gallery](https://datasketch.caesarmar.io/index.md): Published lesson index and original source links.
- [Newsletter](https://datasketch.caesarmar.io/newsletter/index.md): Signup information and email frequency.
- [Newsletter privacy](https://datasketch.caesarmar.io/privacy/index.md): Subscription data and privacy choices.
- [Backfill Playbook: From Request to Release](https://datasketch.caesarmar.io/sketches/backfill-playbook/index.md): A five-stage backfill workflow covering scope, strategy, partitioned runs, validation gates, and atomic publishing.
- [Join Duplication Debugging Workflow](https://datasketch.caesarmar.io/sketches/join-duplication-debugging/index.md): Steps for tracing inflated metrics through row counts, join keys, table grain, join type, and null behavior.
- [Full Refresh vs Incremental Load](https://datasketch.caesarmar.io/sketches/full-refresh-vs-incremental-load/index.md): A comparison of full refresh and incremental loading across data volume, refresh cost, watermarks, late updates, and upserts.
- [Bronze, Silver, and Gold Data Layers](https://datasketch.caesarmar.io/sketches/bronze-silver-gold/index.md): An overview of how Bronze, Silver, and Gold layers move data from raw ingestion through cleaning and standardization to business-ready datasets.
- [Safe Publish Pattern Flow](https://datasketch.caesarmar.io/sketches/safe-publish-pattern/index.md): A staging-first publish flow covering validation checks, a failure gate, atomic publishing where supported, and monitoring after release.
- [A Simple Reconciliation Workflow](https://datasketch.caesarmar.io/sketches/reconciliation-workflow/index.md): Trace source and target count differences through date ranges, filters, grain, keys, pipeline stages, and late updates.
- [Late-Arriving Data](https://datasketch.caesarmar.io/sketches/late-arriving-data/index.md): Five causes of late-arriving data: historical edits, backdated transactions, batch uploads, API or network lag, and delayed source systems.
- [Data Freshness](https://datasketch.caesarmar.io/sketches/data-freshness/index.md): Check timestamps, expected partitions, row volume, source delays, and the freshness SLA before treating a successful pipeline run as ready.
- [Partitioning: Why Scanning Less Data Matters](https://datasketch.caesarmar.io/sketches/partitioning/index.md): How partitioning can reduce scanning work when a query skips irrelevant partitions, and why runtime and cost benefits depend on the workload.

## Author source

- [Mario Caesar portfolio](https://caesarmar.io/index.md): Public professional background and attribution source.
